title: Water treatment plant: clean an RO train in place

p: Clean RO train B with the CIP skid (
): a high-pH cleaning, then a low-pH one, the wastes neutralised in the pit before they are discharged.

text: ) came off line for its cleaning: its normalised permeate flow (
) is down to 89 %, more than 10 % under its clean value. RO A carries the plant meanwhile.

p: Normalised flow corrects the permeate flow for temperature and pressure: a fall of 10 %, a rise of 5–10 % in salt passage or of 15 % in differential pressure calls for a cleaning ([FT] §6.3).
Permeate, free of chlorine and hardness: tap or filtered water would scale or oxidise the membranes.

text: Dose caustic soda into the tank (0.1 % NaOH, pH 12) and start its heater (
): the solution must be at pH 11.5–12 and 30–35 °C.

p: High pH first: it takes off the colloids, the organics and the biofilm, which an acid would only fix to the membrane. Warm it works faster, but polyamide takes pH 12 only up to 35 °C.

text: ) with the high-pH solution: the CIP pump (
) recirculates it through the first stage, then the second, the elements soak, and permeate flushes the solution to the neutralisation pit.

p: One stage at a time, at 6–10 m³/h a vessel and under 4 bar: the flow lifts the foulant off the membranes without pressing it in. About two and a half hours of the clock.

p: Low pH takes off the scale (calcium carbonate, metal oxides) the antiscalant did not hold back.

text: ) with the low-pH solution: the CIP pump (
) recirculates it through the first stage, then the second, the elements soak, and permeate flushes the solution to the neutralisation pit.

p: One stage at a time, at 6–10 m³/h a vessel and under 4 bar: the flow lifts the foulant off the membranes without pressing it in. About two and a half hours of the clock.

text: ) is back above 98 %: the train is clean and ready as the standby train.

p: A cleaning restores most of the flow, never all of it: what is left builds up over the membranes' life until they are replaced.

text: Start the neutralisation batch at the pit (
): the caustic and acid wastes are dosed to pH 6.5–8.5, mixed and checked, then discharged.

p: The two wastes partly neutralise each other; the acid's is the larger, so the batch doses caustic. The discharge is allowed only between pH 6 and 9.
